## Reconciled October14 status

The compact status/connection-readiness implementation exists. EN/FR component controls and actual installed bridge tests through WebKit navigation pass: both typed values arrive, status remains connected and keyboard geometry remains fixed. Reviewed narrow/wide frames and canonical references are retained. This supersedes the earlier unimplemented-ribbon description.

Remaining: final-source integration and affected assembled-image/retained regression; no physical-phone or screen-reader claim. Evidence: local `docs/qa-logs/2026-10-13-setup-qualification/installed/README.md`, source-bound frame index and original receipts. Earlier component failures remain failures; no acceptance is inferred for a different final composition.

This is a scoped readiness update under #585; all broader unproved acceptance criteria remain open. Earlier sections below retain their dated source/evidence history.

## Earlier intake and evidence history

Keep the phone keyboard's connection status truthful and stable while the handheld browser navigates or reloads. A page transition alone must not imply that the phone's control session disconnected. Replace the full-width status ribbon with a fixed-size status glyph at the header's top right, keeping the service heading at top left. Ellipsize long service names, retain accessible state descriptions and avoid vertical layout jumps. Distinguish connected, disconnected and warning states without relying only on color.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. Exercise a synthetic browser through reloads, navigation and delayed page completion, then genuine bridge failure/recovery and session end. Use phone-sized browser frames as well as relevant VM flow evidence; no owner device input or screenshot is required.

- [x] Trace status lifecycle and separate page loading from a genuine control-session failure; preserve useful feedback on real failure.
- [x] Fixed header glyph has accessible state text, readable long-name truncation and stable keyboard/control positions through transitions.
- [x] Synthetic navigation, failure/reconnect and ended-session controls verify behavior; reviewed narrow/wide EN/FR frames and canonical flow/IA references accompany source changes.
- [x] Verify input and touch/pointer behavior remain usable, with no extra scrolling or focus loss introduced by status updates.

Related #570 performance investigation; requested implementation after #565–#567 and before another candidate build. Original owner wording is retained privately.
